$comment: IPF competition rules, as far as an attempt planner has to know them,
transcribed from the technical rulebook cited in `rulebook`.
THIS PROFILE IS WHY THERE IS NO UNIVERSAL PROFILE.
Read against the USPA profile beside it, this one differs on the opener-change
deadline (three minutes and three attempts, not five and five), on whether a
third-deadlift change is floored by the preceding lifter's weight (it is not),
on how a tie on total is broken after bodyweight (whoever reached the total
first, rather than a reweigh), and -- most consequentially -- on whether fourth
attempts exist at all. They do not. A planner that assumed federations share
these rules would be wrong four times over on one screen.
`fourthAttempt` IS null, NOT A BLOCK OF ZEROES.
The rulebook has no fourth attempt: records are taken on any of the three
prescribed attempts. A zeroed rule block would render as a fourth attempt
nobody may take, which is a different and wrong statement, and it would put a
row on screen that sends a lifter to ask about something that does not exist.
HOW THIS WAS VERIFIED, 2026-08-01
1. The rulebook PDF downloaded, digested, and read as text with `pdftotext
-layout`. `rulebook.sha256` is the digest of those exact bytes.
2. Each figure read back against the lettered rule it came from, listed in
`provenance.sections`.
3. The absence of fourth attempts confirmed by searching the whole document
for 'fourth' and '4th'. Neither appears in the attempt rules. An absence
asserted from a skim is how a federation ends up with a rule this project
invented for it.
4. Absence checked for second-attempt and third-squat changes too: rule (k)
states outright that they cannot be changed.
THE PDF IS NOT COMMITTED. `rulebook.sha256` pins the bytes and `check:upstream`
re-downloads and re-digests them on a schedule, so a revision announces itself
without the document being redistributed. This matters more here than usual:
the pinned edition takes effect on a date, and a build that hard-coded any of it
would go wrong on a day nobody set a reminder for.
label: IPF

rulebook.$comment: `revision` is the effective date and version the document prints on its cover. `sha256` is the digest of the exact bytes read and is what actually detects a change.

openerChange.summary: One change to the first attempt of each lift. In the first group of a session, up to within three minutes of the start of that lift's first round. In a later group, up to within three attempts of the end of the previous group's last round.

thirdAttemptChanges.$comment: `notBelowPrecedingLifter` is false, and the difference from the USPA profile is deliberate. This rulebook states the rising-bar principle without attaching it to the third-deadlift change, and inventing the attachment would have the planner refuse a change an IPF expeditor would accept.

formatOverrides.summary: In a single-lift bench press, two changes are permitted in the third round, on the same rules as the third deadlift.

notes: The submission clock for a second or third attempt starts when the referees' lights are activated on the preceding attempt.
An attempt cannot be withdrawn once it has been turned in.
A missed attempt may be repeated, but only in the next round; a lifter never follows themselves.
There are no fourth attempts. A record may be taken on any of the three prescribed attempts.
A record attempt may be a weight that is not a multiple of 2.5 kg, and only for a record in the championship being competed in. Every other attempt must be a multiple of 2.5 kg.
Where proper notice of an opener-change deadline was not given, an announcement may reopen changes for one further minute.
